name: OAuthAppSpec
description: OAuthAppSpec defines a registered OAuth application with an external vendor.

fields.name: Provider
fields.description:
Human-readable vendor name for UI display and logging.
 Examples: "Slack", "Salesforce", "Figma"

fields.name: ClientId
fields.description: OAuth client identifier registered with the vendor.

fields.name: ClientSecret
fields.description:
OAuth client secret registered with the vendor.
 Encrypted at rest, redacted in logs.

fields.name: AuthorizationUrl
fields.description:
Vendor's OAuth authorization endpoint.
 The browser redirects here to start the authorization code flow.
 Example: "https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize"

fields.name: TokenUrl
fields.description:
Vendor's OAuth token endpoint.
 The backend exchanges the authorization code for tokens here.
 Example: "https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access"

fields.name: Scopes
fields.description:
OAuth scopes to request during the authorization flow.
 Scope values are vendor-specific.
 Examples: ["channels:read", "chat:write"] (Slack),
           ["read_api", "api"] (GitLab)

fields.name: UserinfoUrl
fields.description:
Optional OIDC UserInfo endpoint for fetching user profile data.
 When set, Stigmer calls this endpoint after token acquisition to
 retrieve the user's display name and avatar for the connected account.
 Omit for vendors that do not support a standard userinfo endpoint.

fields.name: ScopeParameterName
fields.description:
Name of the query parameter used to send scopes in the authorization URL.

 Most OAuth providers use the standard "scope" parameter. Some vendors
 use a non-standard name — for example, Slack's V2 OAuth API requires
 user token scopes to be sent as "user_scope" instead of "scope".

 When empty, defaults to "scope" (standard OAuth 2.0 behavior).

fields.name: VendorApprovalStatus
fields.description:
Vendor marketplace/app-review approval status for this OAuth app.

 Many vendors (Slack, Figma, Salesforce, etc.) require an approval
 process before a third-party OAuth app can be used publicly. This
 field tracks where Stigmer's registration stands with the vendor.

 UNSPECIFIED is treated as approved for backwards compatibility — only
 apps explicitly marked PENDING are gated in the UI.

fields.name: VendorApprovalDocsUrl
fields.description:
Documentation URL explaining how users can bring their own OAuth
 app credentials or personal access tokens for this vendor while
 the platform's OAuth app is pending approval.

 Shown in the frontend as a help link when vendor_approval_status
 is PENDING. Empty means no documentation link is displayed.

fields.name: TokenEndpointAuthMethod
fields.description:
How the client secret is presented to the vendor's token endpoint
 during authorization-code exchange and refresh.

 RFC 6749 §2.3.1 requires authorization servers to support HTTP Basic,
 but some vendors' token endpoints accept only client_secret_post
 (e.g. HubSpot advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported:
 ["client_secret_post"]). Exactly one method is ever used per request —
 RFC 6749 §2.3 forbids presenting credentials through more than one
 channel at once, and some servers reject requests that do.

 UNSPECIFIED is treated as CLIENT_SECRET_BASIC for backwards
 compatibility, preserving the historical behavior byte-for-byte.
